entries.finding: A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 human studies found no significant overall effect of curcumin on global cognitive outcomes, indicating that broad cognition claims remain inconsistent.
The same 2025 synthesis found a significant improvement in working memory in subgroup analysis, suggesting effects may be domain-specific rather than global.
The 2025 cognition meta-analysis reported a significant improvement in processing speed, while overall global cognition remained null.

The 2025 cognition synthesis reported a higher incidence of adverse events in the curcumin group than in controls, reinforcing the need to distinguish potential cognitive benefit from tolerability evidence.
A 2025 meta-analysis of 14 randomized trials in postmenopausal women found curcumin was associated with lower systolic blood pressure versus control.
The same postmenopausal-women meta-analysis found a significant reduction in diastolic blood pressure with curcumin supplementation.
Curcumin increased total antioxidant capacity in the 2025 postmenopausal-women meta-analysis, providing biomarker evidence rather than a direct symptom outcome.
The 2025 synthesis reported an improvement in vasomotor symptoms among postmenopausal women receiving curcumin.

A 2026 network meta-analysis of 29 randomized trials involving 2,107 healthy adults ranked high-dose Bacopa monnieri among the strongest interventions for working memory, though the authors noted limits from the indirect nature of comparisons.

The 2026 network meta-analysis reported greater short-term-memory benefit with high-dose Bacopa monnieri than comparator groups, while emphasizing that evidence came largely from indirect network comparisons.
No significant differences were observed for sustained attention, selective attention, or processing speed in the 2026 Bacopa-versus-Ginkgo network meta-analysis.

In a 2025 randomized double-blind trial of 101 healthy adults, Bacopa monnieri did not improve the prespecified primary cognition outcomes but did reduce self-reported stress reactivity as a secondary outcome.
The same 2025 Bacopa trial reported lower fatigue and stress after a cognitively demanding task, while measured blood biomarkers did not differ between groups.
